source_evidence: Consider the size of your investment, how long you expect to own the mutual fund and your need to access the money you invested when you think of the trade-off between share classes that charge front-end sales loads, CDSLs, and ongoing fees.
question: Misconception: “The size of my investment matters, but how long I hold a mutual fund share class does not affect which fee structure is suitable.”
answer: Holding period matters too. Compare the trade-off between front-end sales loads, contingent deferred sales loads (CDSLs), and ongoing fees in light of your investment size, expected holding period, and need to access the money. A class with lower initial fees may not have the lowest fees over time.
